summary: Frontend E2E validated end-to-end via Playwright against the public preview URL. All 6 requested flows pass: (1) invalid URL shows red error banner with data-testid='error-message'; (2) scraping the specified Cricbuzz URL renders match_title, venue/toss meta, batting table with 7 columns and bowling table with 8 columns; (3) innings-tab-1 switches batting/bowling content (verified batting first row changed from 'Pawantha Weerasinghe' to 'Sai Sudharsan'); (4) Download CSV triggers GET /api/scorecards/{id}/csv returning 200; (5) new history-item-{id} appears in sidebar and clicking it reloads the preview; (6) history-item-delete-{id} with accepted confirm removes the item and clears the currently-open preview.
critical_code_review_comments: Scrape button remains disabled while URL input is empty, so the 'empty URL' branch of handleScrape ('Please enter a URL.') is unreachable from the UI. The message is dead code; consider either removing the disabled state or removing the empty-string branch to keep behaviour consistent with the exposed UX.

handleDownload uses axios with responseType blob and a synthetic anchor click; works fine but the browser download itself cannot be asserted by Playwright without expect_download. The /api/scorecards/{id}/csv 200 response was verified instead, which is the correct proxy.
openHistoryItem sets url from the history item, which is helpful UX, but does not scroll to preview; low priority.
seed_data_creation: One Cricbuzz scorecard was scraped and then deleted as part of the test; other pre-existing history items remain untouched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend validation, preview rendering, innings tab switching, CSV download, and history reload/delete all work. The regression fix (text input + client-side validation) is verified: entering 'not-a-valid-url' produces the red error banner 'URL must start with http:// or https://'. Scrape button is disabled when input is empty, so the 'Please enter a URL.' error is unreachable from the UI (minor dead-code note only).
